terms.definition: An installable unit with a plugin.json: its pages, sections, settings and declarations.
A native program of one domain with a sidecar.json that plugin pages talk to.

The file that sok plugin pack or sok sidecar release writes and that a registry lists: <id>-<version>.tgz of a plugin, <file name>-<version>-<platform>.tar.gz of a sidecar, or soksak-<version>-<platform>-<host>.zip of an application bundle.
The folder that plugins/installed.json records for an installed plugin.
A document of a plugin that a document region shows at sok://<plugin id>/<path>.
An address soksak://<owner>/<command> that opens from outside the application.
The file logs/application.log under the configuration directory: the host lines, the page lines sent through report, and the standard error of the sidecars that the host starts.
The events page.trace.*, host.trace.*, host.sampler.* and sidecar trace events that the layers store in the event files under logs/ while the setting diagnostics.performance is on.
A file logs/state-<time>.json that the debug view writes: the state of the host, the versions and every window at one time.
The dialog that Help > Debug opens: it records a state file, lists the files of logs/ and saves them.
One record of the contract in docs/spec/logging.md: a JSON object with a time, a sequence number, a level, a layer, a declared name and fields.
The declared kind of an event (lifecycle, input, call, io, frame) that decides how the writer stores it.
The identifier that one native input receives from the layer that first sees it and that every later layer carries (cids in an event).

The rules by language that list each source of occurrences (an empty catch, a discarded result, a goroutine, a registered observer, an error return) and require an event in its function or a reason marker.
The one comment form (default|silent): <reason> that states why a source of occurrences stores no event.
Rebuilding the screen of a terminal session from its stored inputs with the replay executable of its sidecar, to compare the stored hashes of the screens (docs/spec/replay.md).
The events of the layer sidecar that one run (boot) of a sidecar produced for one session; its sequence restarts at 1, and a replay compares each segment on its own (docs/spec/replay.md#segments).
The SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of a terminal screen that docs/spec/replay.md defines; a sidecar and a page store it per frame record.
